description: This syllabus typically covers fundamental concepts of signal processing and system analysis, with applications in robotic control, sensor processing, and automation. This course is a supplementary course for Robotics and Automation Engineers to acquire the skills to handle the ever-increasing automation in different domains.

syllabus.title: Signals and Systems Fundamentals
syllabus.body: Basic definitions and terminology, Classification of signals and systems, Continuous-time and discrete-time signals, Signal operations: shifting, scaling, and reversal, System properties: linearity, time-invariance, causality, stability.

syllabus.title: LTI Systems and Fourier Series
syllabus.body: Continuous and discrete time LTI systems: response using convolution integral/sum, Properties of LTI systems, Modeling of continuous and discrete time LTI systems. Fourier series: representation of continuous and discrete time periodic signals, convergence, properties, Application to LTI systems. Fourier transform: introduction, representation of continuous and discrete time aperiodic and periodic signals, convergence, properties, Application to LTI systems.

syllabus.title: Laplace Transform and Z-Transform
syllabus.body: Laplace transform and its inverse, region of convergence, relation with Fourier transform, properties, Application to LTI systems, their interconnections and block diagram. Z-transform and its inverse, region of convergence, relation with Fourier transform, properties, Application to LTI systems, their interconnections and block diagram.

syllabus.title: Sampling and Applications in Robotics and Automation
syllabus.body: Sampling of continuous time signals, sampling theorem, reconstruction, effect of under sampling. Applications in Robotics and Automation: Signal processing in robotic vision and sensors, control, filtering and noise reduction in automation, Speech and image processing in human-robot interaction and various other sustainable technologies with the inclusion of some case studies from the Indian knowledge system.

outcomes: Characterize and analyze the properties of continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems.
Represent continuous-time and discrete-time systems in the frequency domain using Fourier analysis and solve LTI problems.
Analyze continuous-time and discrete-time systems using Laplace transforms and Z-transforms.
Practice different systems in various applications.
